**(b)** Explain why $\binom{n}{r}=\binom{n}{n-r}$. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Row 4 is $1,4,6,4,1$: $a^{4}+4a^{3}b+6a^{2}b^{2}+4ab^{3}+b^{4}$ **(A2)**

**(b)** Choosing $r$ objects to include from $n$ is the same as choosing the $n-r$ objects to leave out, so both counts are equal (Pascal's triangle is symmetric). **(R1)**
